The buoys need to be repositioned because the riverbed changes over time, so the fairway markings are reviewed each spring. Prior to Russia's full-scale invasion into Ukraine, the buoys were installed largely by mutual agreement. However, starting in 2023, Russia has not agreed with Estonia’s position regarding the placement of buoys. This year, Russia said it disagreed with the location of about half of the planned 250 floating markers. Estonia has installed light buoys in Estonian waters based on the State Border Act and the locations of the buoys that were mutually agreed between border agencies in 2022. "We decided to install floating signs for the summer season in accordance with the agreement of 2022 because they are needed to avoid navigation errors so that our fishermen and vacationers do not accidentally enter Russian waters," Purgel explained.
